note: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2024) specifically describe short midbrain (38%) and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38%) alongside corpus callosum anomalies rather than generalized pontocerebellar hypoplasia.

evidence.text: Neuroimaging in individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants identified midline and posterior fossa malformations including short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis in 38% each, clava hypertrophy in 24%, corpus callosum abnormalities in 70%, and hypoplasia or agenesis of the anterior commissure in 66%.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38% each) as well as hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings.

evidence.text: Review of novel genetic chorea etiologies highlights bi-allelic loss-of-function variants in ACBD6 characterized by chorea along with anterior commissure hypoplasia or agenesis, short midbrain, and small cerebellar vermis.

source.title: Update on Genetic Chorea
